# Agent session: full log

The Claude Code session that built TwoToe, from 2026-10-22 to 2026-10-23: 37 user messages, 1062 tool calls. Claude Code ran natively on Windows (PowerShell), one phase at a time with a stop at every gate (docs/SPEC.md section 16).

Every message and tool call. Tool results are trimmed to 1,200 characters, edits to their first lines.

Redacted for publication: home paths and the user name (`<user>`, `~`), the host name (`<host>`), email addresses, Sentry DSNs and key-like tokens, this machine's repo and projects folder paths (`<repo>`, `<projects>`), and one listing of the user's other project folders. Claude's internal reasoning blocks, system reminders and images are not included. Generated by `scripts/blog/export-session.ts`.

### User (2026-10-22 09:00 UTC)

> You are building TwoToe for the DEV Hacktoberfest Week 3 challenge. The full spec is in
> docs/SPEC.md (PDF copy at docs/SPEC.pdf) and the working agreement is CLAUDE.md.
> Read CLAUDE.md, then SPEC sections 0 through 7 carefully. Before writing any code:
> 1. Summarize the product, the hard rules, and the phase plan back to me in under 200 words.
> 2. List every VERIFY item you see and how you plan to check each (which URL).
> 3. List any spec ambiguity you want me to decide.
> Then wait for my "go". After "go", execute Phase 0 exactly as written in section 16,
> stop at Gate 0, and report. Do not start Phase 1 until I approve.
> Ground rules: never invent advisory facts, never weaken a hard rule to make a test pass,
> and tell me plainly when something failed.
> 
> 
>  work till gate 0 and lemme know when you are done till then

# TwoToe research brief (Oct 22, 2026)

Four research agents ran in parallel: challenge rules and past winners, a fact-check of the Oct 21 incidents, a scan of competing Week 3 entries, and a red-team of SPEC.md. Raw reports with every source URL are in `docs/research/`. This file is the synthesis plus the proposed spec changes. Nothing in SPEC.md has been changed yet.

## 1. Verdict

The idea is still worth building, but the pitch has to move.

- **Still open:** no Week 3 entry targets the Oct 21 breach week. DEV posts on it so far are explainers and checklists, not tools.
- **Already taken:** "code owns facts, a validator rejects model text" is not novel in this challenge. Sloth SOC (nightly log triage, grounding validator, loopback-only egress, red-team table) and MorningDrop already use it, and the Week 1 overall winner Paper Trail was built on it.
- **New headline:** "half of breach week had no package to scan". Railway env vars, OpenCode keys, eMudhra trust, installed Plex, and `.pth` persistence are invisible to osv-scanner, npm audit and pip-audit. TwoToe checks the machine, not just the lockfile, and never reads a secret value.

**Root CA name:** The article never names the root. It refers only to "the eMudhra root" and "the eMudhra CS root." The eight affected intermediates are:
- EM DV TLS CA - G3B and G3C
- EM EV TLS CA - G3B and G3C
- EM OV TLS CA - G3B and G3C
- EM OV CS CA - G3B and G3C

**Number of intermediate keys:** Eight. Each was also cross-signed by Sectigo's AAA Certificate Services root in May 2025.

**Distrust by browsers and vendors:**
- Chrome pushed a CRLSet update blocking the intermediates on the evening of Saturday 17 October. Chrome also confirmed the root is going in Chrome Root Store v43.
- Firefox blocked them via OneCRL a few hours later. Mozilla announced publicly on 20 October and shipped an NSS update removing the root.
- Microsoft's action and date are not mentioned.

**Non-browser clients:** Still trusted by default. The author found that with default settings, "curl said SSL certificate verify ok, Python completed the handshake, and Node said authorized: true" on every Linux and macOS machine tested. On Windows, CryptoAPI accepted the chain unless revocation checking was enabled.

**Bug title:** "eMudhra: Private key compromise of Intermediate Certificates" (the original title was "Private key compromise of eMudhra Intermediate Certificates").

**Root CA names:** The page doesn't fully reconcile the names. Mozilla's emergency distrust targets **"emSign ECC Root CA - G3"** (Comment 18). The eight compromised intermediates are listed under **emSign Root TLS CA - G3** (TLS) and **emSign Root CS CA - G3** (code signing) (Comment 0). Sectigo's cross-signed intermediates chain through a Sectigo-operated root named AAA Certificate Services (Comments 6 and 25).

**Intermediate keys affected:** Eight. Six are TLS intermediates and two are code signing. Eight Sectigo cross-signed certificates also carry these keys, and Sectigo has since revoked them (Comments 0, 2, 13).

**Nature of the weakness:** According to Mozilla's analysis, the P-384 private keys were tiny integers (all below 256), so they could be recovered almost instantly. eMudhra attributes this to a flaw in its April 30, 2025 key generation ceremony, where a weaker second key pair was created and mistakenly used to produce the CSRs (Comments 5, 11).

### Claude (2026-10-22 09:10 UTC)

I've finished Phase 0 and stopped at Gate 0. Phase 1 waits for your approval. Your "work till gate 0" message counted as the "go", so the pre-code summary, the VERIFY list and the open questions are all included here.

## 1. Summary (under 200 words)
TwoToe is a local tool that does breach-week triage overnight. At 7 a.m. it gives you two lines plus a checklist of at most 7 items. Code collects the facts: the probe and scanners build an inventory, and a deterministic matcher turns it into findings with a confidence tier. Local Gemma (via Ollama) only phrases those findings. A validator rejects any token the matcher did not establish, and a template writer is always available as a fallback.

**Hard rules:**
- Env key names only, never values. The canary must never appear in output.
- IOC files get stat and SHA-256 only, never opened or run.
- No installs and no user code during a scan. execFile with argument arrays and 5s timeouts.
- Network goes through an allowlist: loopback, cisa.gov, and Sentry only if you opt in.
- Defensive only.
- Demos and eval use fixtures only, and home paths are redacted to `~`.
- Never edit `expected.json` to make metrics pass.
- Pack facts must come from sources I actually fetched.

**Phases:** 0 scaffold and pack, 1 probe and scanners, 2 matcher and `brief --no-llm`, 3 writer, validator and egress guard, 4 Temporal, 5 card, 6 eval, 7 Sentry, 8 post, 9 stretch. Each phase ends at a gate.

## 2. VERIFY items
I fetched the pages myself and checked each value. The full table, with every URL, is in `docs/VERIFY.md`. Where the spec was wrong, the pack uses the source's value:

- **GitLab CVE-2026-110264:** fixed in 19.5.1, 19.4.3, 19.3.6, 19.2.9, 19.1.9, 19.0.10 and 18.11.13.
- **GitLab CVE-2026-97229:** affects only 19.2 to 19.4. The "commit CI config to a public project" precondition isn't in GitLab's post, so I dropped it.
- **KEV status:** PHP and both GitLab CVEs are not in KEV catalog 2026.10.21. Plex is in KEV, with CVE-2026-96654 and -96656 due Oct 23 and CVE-2026-96652 and -96655 due Nov 3.
- **certifi:** the fixed version is **2026.10.18**.
- **LiteLLM:** Wiz publishes per-OS SHA-256 hashes for the IOC files, so I added them. I dropped "hourly backdoor" because Wiz contradicts itself on which OSes run that script.
- **eMudhra:** I found no source for the "60M certs" figure; the confirmed number is about 30,000 to migrate. Only Mozilla has distrusted the root so far. Chrome's root removal is expected Oct 27.
- **Gemma tag:** `gemma4:e4b` is correct. Cloud tags such as `gemma4:cloud` also exist, so the writer must refuse them.

**Still open:**
- No fetched source says how Microsoft's root block shows up in the Windows store. The pack value is `VERIFY`.
- The OpenCode config folder on Windows (pack value `VERIFY`).
- OpenCode and SBI rest on secondary sources only. The SBI filing PDF on BSE returned HTTP 403.

## 3. Decisions for you
1. **RESEARCH.md P1 to P10 aren't applied** (CLAUDE.md says to ask before changing the spec). Two of them block Phase 1:
   - **P9:** a written exception to rule 1 so the probe can read the values of `APPDATA`, `LOCALAPPDATA`, `USERPROFILE` and `PATH`. Without it, Phase 1 can't find Python or Plex.
   - **P7:** security fixes, such as a stricter key regex, absolute exe paths and no `NODE_OPTIONS` when spawning.
2. **Deadline:** the DEV API closes on Oct 25 at 12:29 PM IST, a day before the rules page. Should we plan for the earlier one?
3. **eMudhra subjects:** match only "emSign ECC Root CA - G3", or also the "Root TLS CA - G3" and "Root CS CA - G3" names from Bugzilla?
4. **kev-recent:** the schema has no "varies" severity, so I set `high`. The window is 7 days in 7.2 and 14 days in 7.5; I used 14.
5. **Secondary sources:** are they good enough for OpenCode and SBI?
6. **CI:** keep the Ubuntu job as the spec says, or cut it as RESEARCH suggests?

## Gate 0
- **Tests:** `pnpm -r test` passes, 40 of 40. Typecheck exits 0 on TypeScript 7.0.2, and I confirmed it does flag errors.
- **Pack:** validates against the zod schema and has exactly the 11 ids from 7.2. A test fails if a `VERIFY` value in the pack is missing from `docs/VERIFY.md`.
- **Tree:** follows 5.1. Later-phase files are placeholders containing only `export {}`. I added `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (Windows and Ubuntu), `.gitattributes`, `.env.example`, a README skeleton with the Week 3 note, and `docs/VERIFY.md`.
- **Privacy sweep:** no home paths, and the canary appears only in tests.

## Things that differ from the spec or need your attention
- **Your Node is v24.11.0, below the patched 24.22.1.** Please upgrade. I didn't add an `engines` field because pnpm would refuse to install on your current Node. `.nvmrc` and CI pin 24.22.1, but I haven't checked that `setup-node` can download that release yet.
- **pnpm:** version 12 fails under your corepack 0.34, so I pinned 11.28.7. It isn't on PATH. Run `corepack enable` once from an admin terminal, or prefix commands with `corepack`, e.g. `corepack pnpm install`.
- **esbuild install script:** pnpm 11 blocks it by default. I declined it explicitly so that no dependency install scripts run. Tests are unaffected.
- **zod:** I used 3.25.76 instead of 4, because section 6's `z.record(z.any())` only works in v3.
- **Small additions to section 6:** an `AdvisoryPack` wrapper schema that rejects duplicate ids. Each advisory also lists its detectors in `params.detectors`, because some advisories need more than one.
- **No commits yet.** Tell me if you want the scaffold committed, or I can do it once you approve Gate 0.

### Claude (2026-10-22 09:33 UTC)

Phase 1 is done and I've stopped for review. All 161 tests pass (153 in core, 8 in the CLI), typecheck is clean, and the real scan is under 20s with no secret values in its output. One caveat: **`~\code` doesn't exist on your machine**, so the scan walked no project files and only the machine-level checks ran.

## Ready-to-go check
Nothing from Gate 0 blocked Phase 1:
- **Reading env values (P9):** not needed. Paths come from your home directory and fixed defaults. Each tool's location is looked up with `where.exe`, and the tool then runs with an empty environment from an empty temp folder.
- **Security fixes (P7):** I applied the parts that only make the rules stricter. `NODE_OPTIONS` can never reach a child process (there's a test for this), and PHP runs as `php -n -v`.
- **The other Gate 0 questions** (deadline, eMudhra names, KEV window, CI matrix) are still open, but none of them affect scanners.

## What the real scan found (paths redacted)
- **Node:** your default `node` is 24.11.0, below the fixed 24.22.1. TwoToe also prints a loud warning because it is running on that Node itself.
- **Python:** 269 packages across 3 locations: `~\AppData\Local\Programs\Python\Python314` (246), `Python312` (1), and `~\AppData\Roaming\Python\Python314` (22). No litellm, and no IOC files.
- **eMudhra root ("emSign ECC Root CA - G3"):** present in your Node 24.11.0 store, in the Python314 `certifi` bundle (certifi 2026.2.25, older than the fixed 2026.10.18), and in the Git for Windows bundle. It is not in the Windows Root or Disallowed stores.
- **OpenCode:** `opencode` is on PATH, and `~\.config\opencode` and `~\.local\share\opencode` exist.
- **Not found:** Railway, PHP and Plex. Docker isn't installed.
- **Privacy checks on the full output:** no canary, no home path, no `C:\Users` string.
- **Timing:** 1.1s wall time, 16 checks. That says nothing about walk speed, because there was nothing to walk.

## What was built
- **Probes:** the `SystemProbe` interface; `RealProbe`, implemented for Windows with simple macOS and Linux branches; and `FixtureProbe`, which reads a zod-validated `probe.json`.
- **Scanners:** every scanner in 8.2, plus a walker that never follows symlinks or junctions, skips OneDrive folders, and counts locked files instead of crashing. `collectInventory` returns an Inventory that passes the schema.
- **CLI:** `twotoe scan [roots] --json --fixture <dir>`.
- **Tests:** everything section 15 lists for Phase 1:
  - the canary never appears in output, logs or errors;
  - `export KEY=`, quoted values, comments, CRLF and a BOM all parse correctly;
  - EBUSY, EPERM and EACCES files are skipped and counted;
  - a 10 MB file is streamed rather than read whole;
  - IOC files are never read as text (checked by spying on the file-reading functions) and their hashes are correct;
  - dist-info folder names parse, with a METADATA fallback;
  - the depth limit holds, and junction loops end without double-counting.

## Bugs the tests and the real run caught (all fixed)
1. pnpm lockfile keys with a peer suffix like `(foo@1.0.0)` were parsed with the wrong name.
2. Redaction turned the short path `~ into `~~1`.
3. The Git for Windows bundle writes names as `# emSign ECC Root CA - G3`, which my search missed. That made a false "not present" on your machine; it now correctly reports present.
4. With `| Select-Object -First 50`, the exit code is -1. That is Windows PowerShell 5.1 stopping the program early; a full run exits 0. I also added handling so a closed pipe exits quietly in other shells.

## Where I went beyond the spec text (please confirm)
- **.env parser:** it follows the 8.2.6 algorithm, with two additions so PEM fragments can't come out as key names:
  - It tracks which quote is open, and skips every line inside a multi-line quoted value.
  - It drops long mixed-case "keys" that look like base64. These are counted and reported in the scan stats.
- **Docker Compose `environment:` keys** are read line by line rather than with a YAML parser, so values are never loaded into an object.
- **Skipped-file counts** live in a `stats` object next to the Inventory. Section 5.4 says to put them in `brief.meta`, but the Brief schema has no field for them. That needs deciding in Phase 2 or 3.
- **Package `source` strings** start with `site-packages:`, `pin:` or `lockfile:`, so the matcher can tell installed packages from pins.
- **The Node self-check warns but doesn't refuse to run**, otherwise it would block you today.

## Still unverified
- How Microsoft's block appears in the Windows certificate store (still `VERIFY`).
- The Microsoft Store Python, pipx and uv paths, and Plex's `ProductVersion` format: none of them are installed here.
- Docker running with an empty environment: untested, since Docker isn't installed.

The OpenCode config folder is settled from OpenCode's docs and this machine, and `docs/VERIFY.md` is updated.

**Next steps:**
- Scanning `~\Desktop` (the only default root that exists here) would give a real measurement for the 20s target. Say if you want that.
- Phase 1 isn't committed. I can commit it once you approve.

### Claude (2026-10-22 09:43 UTC)

I fixed both dependency problems. Your Node is now 24.22.1, `pnpm` works directly, and the post material is saved. I'm stopped until you say go.

## Dependencies
- **Node: upgraded from 24.11.0 to 24.22.1.** winget's Node LTS package was still on 24.20.0, which is also unpatched, so I downloaded the official installer from nodejs.org instead. Its checksum matches the published SHA-256 and it carries a valid OpenJS Foundation signature. It installed after you approved the UAC prompt.
- **pnpm: now on PATH, no admin needed.** I put corepack's pnpm shim in your user npm folder. Plain `pnpm ...` now works and uses the pinned 11.28.7.
- **Engines check added:** the root `package.json` now requires a patched Node (`^22.23.4 || ^24.22.1 || >=26.12.1`), so pnpm refuses to install on an older one. I couldn't test the refusal, since I no longer have an unpatched Node to run it on.
- **Verified on the new Node:** install, typecheck and all 161 tests pass. The original command `pnpm tsx packages/cli/src/index.ts scan $HOME\code --json` runs with no Node warning, and the output still has no canary or home path.
- **The upgrade fixed part of the eMudhra exposure:** Node 24.22.1 no longer trusts "emSign ECC Root CA - G3"; 24.11.0 did. The Git for Windows CA bundle and the certifi bundle in one of your Python installs still trust it. Those are checklist items for later phases.

## Saved for the post
- **`docs/post/build-log.md`** (counts only, no machine paths). It covers:

  - the 4 bugs the tests and the real run caught;

  - what the check can't see yet.
- **Session transcript:** Claude Code keeps it automatically under `~\.claude\projects\`. It contains your real paths, so I left it out of the repo. Redact it before using it for "My Agent Session".
- **`docs/VERIFY.md` and the README** are updated with the Node upgrade, the trust store result, and the new pnpm setup steps.

Phase 2 is done and I've stopped at Gate 2. All 20 truth-table rows pass, and `brief --no-llm` prints the section 12 layout.

## Output for the temporary f01 + f06 + f10 + f17 fixture
```
  twotoe  Thu Oct 22, 15:28

  4 things need you today: update Plex to 1.43.3.10861; rebuild your litellm env on 1.106.2; +2 more in the checklist.
  Everything else: you're fine. Checked 14 things in 0.02s, 0 secrets left this machine.

  [ ] 1  Update Plex Media Server from 1.43.3.10860 ...  definite  Plex Media Server
  [ ] 2  Rebuild the env with litellm 1.106.2 and ro...  definite  .venv
  [ ] 3  Roll every env var, API key, and registry c...  likely    railway.toml, .env (RAILWAY_TOKEN)
  [ ] 4  Upgrade Node from 24.22.0 to 24.22.1            definite  node --version

  card: twotoe card (not built yet)   model: none (--no-llm)   validator: not needed
```
- **Exit code 10** is the spec's "actions found" code, not a failure.
- **Order** follows the 7.4 priority scores:

  | Finding | Score | Why |
  |---|---|---|
  | Plex | −5 | critical, in KEV, due Oct 23 |
  | LiteLLM | 70 | critical, definite |
  | Railway | 85 | critical, likely |
  | Node | 170 | high, definite |

- **Privacy:** no canary and no home path in the `--json` output.
- **The fixture** is in the scratchpad, not the repo. Real fixtures with `expected.json` come in Phase 6.

## Tests
236 pass (209 core, 14 writer, 13 CLI), and typecheck is clean. Each truth-table row runs the real pipeline: synthetic files, then scan, then match. Other tests cover:
- the priority formula and the "credential leaks first" tie-break;
- three venvs merging into one finding with three evidence rows;
- GitLab and Plex image tags, Node 20 end-of-life, PHP 8.1 "take offline", and floating Docker tags;
- the KEV matcher;
- line assembly (singular/plural, "+k more", the 160-character limit, the egress clause);
- the Brief schema.

## Real machine (template mode, zero model calls)
- "1 thing needs you today: update certifi and Git for Windows". Your Git for Windows CA bundle and one Python's certifi still trust the eMudhra root.
- OpenCode shows up as a "possible" checklist item.
- 16 checks in 0.7s.

## Decisions I made (please confirm)
1. **Two schema additions:**
   - an optional `Finding.vars` holding the found version, the fixed version and a wording variant (the template in 10.6 needs these, and section 6's Finding has nowhere to put them);
   - `Advisory.shortAction`, which 10.6 asks for.
2. **Wording lives in the pack:** `{found}`/`{fixed}` placeholders, variants (compromised env, take offline, floating tag, Confirm...), and product names for `allowedTokens`. Tests check every action stays within 90 characters and every "possible" wording starts with "Confirm".
3. **`line2Tail`:** 10.7 never uses it. I use it as "Everything else: {tail}." with "you're fine" in template mode.
4. **`twotoe brief` without `--no-llm`** exits 2 and says the model writer arrives in Phase 3, rather than quietly falling back to the template.
5. **Region** comes from `~/.twotoe/config.json`, a fixture's `config.json`, or `--region`, never from an env var.
6. **Node 20 is confirmed end-of-life** on nodejs.org. The wording gives no date, because that page only shows a "last updated" date.

## Open items
- **Needed before Phase 3:** section 10.1 reads `process.env.TWOTOE_MODEL`, which is an env value. May TwoToe read its own `TWOTOE_*` settings, or should the model come from config and `--model` only? Related: the colour library reads `NO_COLOR`/`TERM`.
- **KEV matching is built and tested, but the bundled KEV snapshot is empty.** The KEV refresh (7.5, a SHOULD) hasn't been built.
- **The spec's terminal mockup says "Thu Oct 23"**, but Oct 23, 2026 is a Friday. The code computes the weekday.
- **The action column cuts off at about 46 characters,** as in the mockup, so the end of long actions is hidden. The full text is in `--json` and will be on the card.

`docs/post/build-log.md` and `docs/VERIFY.md` are updated. Nothing is committed. I'm waiting for your go before Phase 3.

### Claude (2026-10-22 10:39 UTC)

Phase 3 is done and I've stopped at Gate 3. All 5 real-model runs on the kitchen-sink fixture passed the validator first time, with only loopback traffic. All 293 tests pass and typecheck is clean.

## The 5 real runs (gemma4:e4b on your RTX 3050)

| Run | Rejections | Final mode | Brief time |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0 | llm | 21.3s |
| 2 | 0 | llm | 22.9s |
| 3 | 0 | llm | 23.2s |
| 4 | 0 | llm | 23.2s |
| 5 | 0 | llm | 23.0s |

- **Every run** sent a 2,619-token prompt and got 438 to 483 tokens back.
- **Egress:** each run made a single 7,905-byte POST to 127.0.0.1 and nothing else. The canary was absent everywhere.
- **The one rejection I saw:** a run just before the final code was rejected for "why over 140 characters" on the Railway item, and fixed on retry (27.2s + 23.0s).

## Things the runs don't hide
- **Runs 2 to 5 were byte-identical** because the spec fixes `seed: 42`. Five runs here are not five independent samples, so the real rejection rate has to come from the Phase 6 eval across 24 fixtures.
- **The model mostly copies the template's wording,** lightly trimmed. Its own contribution was a tail that's a bit off-tone: "you are doing great work". That makes the template vs model comparison in the eval a real question.
- **The validator checks tokens, not meaning.** It would accept a correct version used in the wrong direction, a negation like "you're not affected", or a confident tone on a "possible" item. I've recorded these as known gaps, not fixed them.
- **Latency** is about 23s per brief, mostly reading the 2,600-token prompt.

## What was built
- **Ollama client:** loopback only, JSON-schema `format`, the 10.1 options, 90s timeout. Thinking is off by default, which cut a small test request from 14.9s to 2.1s.
- **Model choice:** `--model`, then `TWOTOE_MODEL`, then config, then `gemma4:e4b`. Cloud tags are refused, and a test proves no other env var is read.
- **Prompts:** 10.2 verbatim plus the 10.4 example. Evidence paths are sent relative to the scanned folders, never with your home path.
- **Validator:** covers every item in 10.5.
- **Retry and fallback:** attempt 1 is validated, attempt 2 gets the rejection reasons, and after that the template replaces only the failing items. Every reason goes into `brief.meta`.
- **Egress guard:** a per-install allowlist covering `fetch`, `http`/`https` and raw sockets. It wraps every `brief` run, template mode included.
- **Tests:** everything section 15 lists for Phase 3, plus a check that every template draft passes the validator.

## Spec deviations (all in `docs/DECISIONS.md`)
- **Stricter CVE pattern:** an invented "CVE-2026-1" slipped past the spec's pattern in a unit test, so it now catches any length.
- **Disclosure dates are allowed tokens.** The spec's own example says "Oct 21", which the validator would otherwise reject.
- **The model sees each finding's `kev` flag,** because rule 4 depends on it.
- **No model call when nothing is found.**
- **No retry when Ollama is down;** it falls back to the template straight away.
- **Code fixes checklist order and line-1 casing** instead of rejecting the draft for them.
- **`.env.example` now lists only `TWOTOE_MODEL`.**

Saved: `docs/post/build-log.md` (Gate 3 numbers and the failures above), `docs/DECISIONS.md`, and the raw run outputs in the scratchpad at `~\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\<project-id>\2cd73442-88f7-48ba-b4cc-f50e5b2d74c3\scratchpad\run5-out`. Nothing is committed.

We're good to go. Waiting for your signal for Phase 4.

Phase 4 is done and I've stopped at Gate 4. The crash test shows **0 activities executed twice**, the nightly schedule shows up on a Temporal server, all 309 tests pass, and typecheck is clean.

## Crash test summary (latest run)
```
TwoToe crash test summary
  workflow                           -> llm, 4 checklist items, 88.4s
  killed                             worker 1, 8s into a 20s delay inside writeBriefWithValidation
  activities completed before crash  3 (collectInventory, loadPack, matchAdvisories)
  activities retried                 1 (writeBriefWithValidation (attempt 2))
  activities executed twice          0   <- must be 0
  model calls / reused from cache    2 / 2
  model requests computed twice      0   <- must be 0
  canary hits in cache, logs, briefs 0
```
I ran it three times against a real dev server and your real gemma4:e4b, with a real `taskkill /PID <pid> /T /F`. All three showed 0 executed twice and 0 model requests computed twice.

## What happened along the way
- **Run 2 exited 1, and my script was at fault, not durability.** The validator rejected that run's first draft (fields too long), so the writer correctly made 2 model calls. Both were reused after the crash, but my script required exactly 1 call. It now checks "no model request computed twice", counted per request.
- **Every run finished at exactly 88.4s,** despite different kill times. The Temporal SDK only passes a heartbeat to the server every 24s (0.8 × the 30s timeout), so recovery is set by the last heartbeat that got through, not by when the worker died.
- **`twotoe sleep` printed your real home path in its first version** (a rule-6 violation). I caught it by reading the output; it's now redacted, with a test.
- **I missed the Temporal CLI** when you asked what to install manually. I installed it with winget: the official 1.9.1, per user, no admin.

## What was built
- **Workflow:** follows 11.3.
- **Six activities:** each is cached on disk per run, keyed by an input hash, so a retry never redoes finished work.
- **Model responses** are cached per request, so a crash after the model answered doesn't ask it again.
- **The inventory and advisory pack** pass between activities as cache references, so Temporal's history database never stores env key names or file paths.
- **Worker** with the egress guard installed; Temporal stays on loopback.
- **Schedule:** daily 03:00 in your timezone, overlap SKIP, 6h catch-up window. Shown on a throwaway server: next run 21:30 UTC, which is 03:00 IST.
- **`twotoe sleep`:** checks for a server and prints the start command if there isn't one. `--taskscheduler` registers the server and worker at logon, `--no-temporal` adds one daily task with WakeToRun and StartWhenAvailable, `--uninstall` removes them all, and `--dry-run` shows the plan.
- **Also added:** a `twotoe worker` command, `brief --save`, an opt-in Windows toast, and the KEV refresh from 7.5 (the workflow calls it).
- **Tests:** TestWorkflowEnvironment covers the happy path, an activity failure followed by a retry, and the schedule.

## Decisions for you
1. **Catch-up window:** I kept the spec's 6h, with a `--catchup` flag. RESEARCH P6 suggests 18h, because a lid kept closed past 9 a.m. would skip that night's run. Should I change the default?
2. **Crash-test kill timing:** the 8s clock starts when the model activity enters the injected delay, not at workflow start. Killing mid-model-call could never show a finished result being reused. The 20s delay and 8s kill are as specified.
3. **Scheduled tasks are not registered on your machine.** Only `--dry-run` was run. Should I register them? (`twotoe sleep --taskscheduler` or `--no-temporal`)

## Not verified
- Whether `conhost --headless` avoids the brief console flash from hidden tasks; I didn't use it.
- The toast pop-up hasn't been seen on screen.
- The KEV refresh hasn't run against the live CISA feed inside a nightly run.

## Before the post
To record the Temporal UI timeline, run `pnpm tsx packages/worker/scripts/crash-test.ts --keep-server`; the dev server stays up at http://127.0.0.1:8233.

Saved: `docs/post/build-log.md` (crash results and the failures above), `docs/DECISIONS.md`, `docs/VERIFY.md`, and the memory notes. Nothing is committed.

We're good to go. Waiting for your signal for Phase 5.

**pnpm:** Yes, pnpm is supported.
- **Detection:** A `pnpm-lock.yaml` at the root alongside `package.json` causes App Platform to use pnpm.
- **Lockfile precedence:** If multiple lockfiles exist, the order is `yarn.lock`, then `pnpm-lock.yaml`, then `package-lock.json`.
- **Version pinning:** You can set the version in the `packageManager` field, which uses Corepack. The page states that "The version defined in `package.json` must be exact." You can also set `engines.pnpm`.

**Build command:** The `build` script in `package.json` runs by default. The page also documents optional hooks: `heroku-prebuild` (before installing dependencies), `heroku-postbuild` (after installing, before pruning), and `heroku-cleanup` (after pruning and caching). ### Claude (2026-10-22 11:28 UTC)

Phase 5 is done and I've stopped at Gate 5. The card scores Lighthouse accessibility 100, fits a 360px phone in both themes, and `twotoe card` serves it locally. The one part of the gate I can't do myself is a live deployment on the `.tech` domain; the config and steps are ready.

## The three decisions (checked against docs first)
1. **Catch-up window: changed to 18h.** Temporal's docs say the window controls how late a missed run may still start after the server was down or asleep, and the default is one year. With the spec's 6h, opening the laptop after 9 a.m. would silently skip that night's brief. 18h still runs it the same day and can't collide with the next night's run.
2. **Crash-test kill timing: kept as is.** Timing the kill from the injected delay is the only way to prove a finished model result gets reused.
3. **Scheduled tasks: not registered yet.** I'd do it at code freeze (Phase 8). Registering now would start half-built code at every log on and fill Temporal's database with dev runs. At freeze, `twotoe sleep --taskscheduler` gives the post real "ran while I slept" numbers.

## The card
- **Design:** the spec's paper and ink palette, with the two lines in Fraunces using its soft-serif setting. The sloth is my own drawing: two toes, closed eyes, swaying gently on its branch, and still when the system asks for reduced motion. Dark mode follows the system setting.
- **Sections:** header with model and mode badge, the two lines, a checklist that remembers ticks per brief date and item, FYI, the network ledger, run stats with the validator's rejections, and the footer. Each checklist item has a confidence chip, evidence rows and vendor advisory links.
- **Colour contrast:** the spec's clay, moss and amber fail accessibility contrast for small text on paper (4.48, 4.10 and 2.65; the minimum is 4.5). I kept them for the big first line, fills and the sloth, and used deeper shades of the same colours for chips and small text.
- **Accessibility:** Lighthouse scored 100 on all three examples in light mode and 100 in dark. There's no sideways scrolling at 360px.
- **Privacy:** fonts are self-hosted, so the hosted page loads nothing from other servers.

## Example briefs
These are real pipeline runs on synthetic fixtures with your local model. Each fixture runs in a throwaway fake home, so paths read `~\code\...`, and the generator refuses to write anything containing the canary or a real path.
- **f22 kitchen sink:** 4 items, accepted on the first try.
- **f06 Railway user:** 1 item; the validator rejected 2 things, then the retry passed.
- **f23 clean night:** "Nothing needs you today.", with no model call.

## `twotoe card`
- Serves the card on 127.0.0.1:4777 from your latest saved brief (`twotoe brief --save`).
- With no saved brief, it shows the examples.
- Loopback only, read-only requests, a strict same-origin security policy, and blocked paths outside the build folder.

## Deployment (DigitalOcean)
- **Why DigitalOcean:** its category text says "host your app", which satisfies the spec's rule.
- **What's ready:** `.do/app.yaml` (repo `T-RexBytes/twotoe`, `twotoe.tech` plus `www`), and `docs/DEPLOY.md` with every step and source URL. DNS is a CNAME to the `…ondigitalocean.app` address, A records for the root domain, and a note about CAA records.
- **Unconfirmed until the first deploy:** that DigitalOcean's build offers Node 24.22.1 yet, and that `node-js` is the right environment name.

## Things I hit along the way
- My first 360px screenshot looked broken. It was headless Chrome's minimum window width on Windows, not the card.
- My first "light" Lighthouse run actually audited dark mode, because Chrome picked up your Windows dark setting. I re-ran with light forced.
- One slip of mine: a messy shell command hung and had to be stopped. It didn't change any files.

## For you
- **Claim `twotoe.tech`** on hacktoberfest.com/my/promos, then follow `docs/DEPLOY.md`. This needs your DigitalOcean and registrar accounts.
- **Then check `https://twotoe.tech` on your phone** to close the gate.

Tests: 328 pass (216 core, 63 writer, 9 worker, 25 CLI, 15 card), and typecheck is clean. Saved: `docs/post/build-log.md`, `docs/DECISIONS.md` (all three decisions with sources), `docs/VERIFY.md`, `docs/DEPLOY.md`, and the README. Nothing is committed.

We're good to go. Waiting for your signal for Phase 6.

### Claude (2026-10-22 13:00 UTC)

The eval results are saved and checked; the matcher scored 20/20, and no invented fact reached a final brief.

**Saved:**
- `eval/RESULTS.md`: every table from 14.3.
- `eval/results.json`: raw data for all 240 briefs, now including the commit, wall time and scan timings.
- `docs/post/build-log.md`: numbers, failures and fix proposals.
- `docs/DECISIONS.md` is updated.
- All 357 tests pass and typecheck is clean. Not committed.

## Results (3 models × 5 runs × 16 fixtures with findings = 240 briefs, 64.7 min)
- **Matcher:** 20/20, 0 false positives, 0 misses (precision and recall 100%). The kitchen-sink order is correct, and the clean machine says "Nothing needs you today."
- **Privacy:** the canary appears nowhere in the outputs, and the only traffic during the whole eval was to 127.0.0.1.
- **Validator:** it rejected 273 of 405 model drafts, and 141 of those had a version, number, CVE or name that code hadn't established for that spot. Most of these are real facts in the wrong section (gemma4:e2b restating checklist facts as FYI) rather than inventions. **None reached a final brief, for any model.**

| Model | Drafts rejected | Briefs needing the template | Median / p90 time | Tokens/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| gemma4:e4b | 43% | 7 of 80 | 15.5 / 20.1 s | 21.3 |
| gemma4:e2b | 96% | 74 of 80 | 6.6 / 11.4 s | 65.9 |
| qwen3:4b | 55% | 27 of 80 | 16.5 / 45.7 s | 12.2 |

gemma4:e4b is the clear default: 9 in 10 of its briefs end up in its own words.

## What went wrong, honestly
- **My first report contradicted itself** ("llm-fallback, fixed on retry") and didn't highlight the offending token, as 14.3 asks. I fixed the report code and re-rendered from the saved data instead of re-running the models.
- **My first re-render also leaked today's commit hash and re-timed the scans.** A diff caught it. Re-rendering now keeps the original values, and the final diff shows only a "re-rendered" note changed; all 240 briefs' data is identical.

## Matcher misses
None. Two caveats:
- **I wrote both the matcher and the expected results,** so 100% is weaker evidence than it looks. Held-out fixtures written first (the research doc's suggestion) would fix that.
- **`kev-recent` has no fixture,** so its zeros mean "not tested", not "perfect".

## Fix proposals (not applied; expected results untouched)
1. **"Why" text over 140 characters (118 rejections):** 9 of 11 pack summaries are longer than 140 characters, and models copy them. Fix: give the model a 140-character limit and the template's already-trimmed sentence as a suggestion.
2. **Wrong number of line-1 actions (131 rejections):** models add an action when only "possible" items exist, or split one action into two. Fix: state the exact count in the prompt, and let code drop extra line-1 actions.
3. **gemma4:e2b fills FYI when there's nothing to say (123 drafts):** code should empty that field when there are no FYI items.
4. **The spec's example leaks into answers:** in 7 drafts, "24.22.1" appeared on non-Node fixtures, and 5 drafts reused its fake ids. Fix: use obviously fake placeholders in the example.

My recommendation is to apply these four and rerun the eval, so the post can report before and after. Say the word and I'll do it.

# Manual Instrumentation Spec: AI Agent Tracing (Node.js)

I've summarized the spec rather than reproducing the code examples in full, because that would quote the source document beyond the 125-character limit.

## Common Rules

- **Span op:** `gen_ai.{operation name}`, e.g. `gen_ai.chat`. Stream mode uses the `sentry.op` attribute instead.
- **Span name:** `{operation} {subject}`, e.g. `invoke_agent Weather Agent`, `chat o3-mini`, `execute_tool get_weather`.
- **Timing:** Set common attributes at span start so sampling can use them. Record accurate start and end times.
- **Errors:** Set status to ERROR and `error.type` to a low-cardinality code or exception class.
- **Complex values:** Messages, tool definitions, and arrays must be JSON strings, since span attributes accept only primitives.
- **Nesting:** `invoke_agent` is the parent. Each model call and tool run is a child. End the model span before running a tool so latency is not mixed.

## Invoke Agent (`gen_ai.invoke_agent`)

- **Name:** `invoke_agent {gen_ai.agent.name}`
- **Required:** `gen_ai.operation.name` = `"invoke_agent"`
- **Recommended:** `gen_ai.agent.name` (string)
- **Optional:**
  - `gen_ai.pipeline.name` (stri

+   return span;

**What `npx @sentry/agent-plugin install none-0un#44aee8d228` does:**
- It installs Sentry's plugin into your AI tools. For Claude Code it runs `claude plugin install sentry@claude-plugins-official`, which adds the Sentry MCP server (`mcp.sentry.dev`). It does the same for Codex, Cursor and Grok if they're installed.
- `none-0un#44aee8d228` is your **org slug** plus a 10-character **onboarding run code**. The installer only puts these into a getting-started prompt it copies to your clipboard, so an agent can report setup progress to Sentry's onboarding page.
- It never outputs a DSN, which is what TwoToe needs to send the trace.
- It's interactive, and the plugin's tools only load after Claude Code restarts, so I couldn't use them in this session anyway.
- It's official: published by `sentry-bot` from `getsentry/sentry-for-ai`.

**What it does give me:** your org slug, so once a trace is sent I can build the link: `https://none-0un.sentry.io/explore/traces/trace/<trace-id>/`.

**Two ways forward:**
1. **Fastest:** copy the DSN from Sentry, either from the onboarding page's "Configure SDK" step or from Settings → Projects → your project → Client Keys (DSN). Paste it here, or add it to `~/.twotoe/config.json` as `{ "telemetry": { "sentry": true, "dsn": "…" } }`.

### Claude (2026-10-22 14:47 UTC)

**Products:**
- **Tracing: yes, required.** The demo trace (scan → match → model attempts → validator) is tracing data, and Sentry's AI agent views are built on it.
- **Error monitoring: optional.** It's harmless to leave on, but TwoToe doesn't send errors, so it won't be used.
- **Logging, Profiling, Application Metrics: no.** TwoToe doesn't send any of these.

**Repository: no, skip it.** It's optional and only adds source context and suspect commits for errors, which we don't send. Skipping it also means Sentry gets no access to your GitHub.

**Two other fields:**
- Platform: Node.js is correct.
- Project name: I'd use `twotoe` instead of `node`, since it appears in Sentry URLs. Team `#none` is fine.

After you create it, the next page shows a code snippet containing a line like `dsn: "https://…@o….ingest….sentry.io/…"`. Copy that DSN and paste it here, or add it to `~/.twotoe/config.json` yourself.

## Gate 7: confirmed
I re-ran the exact demo command with a capture server standing in for Sentry, to see every span actually sent:

- **Still unconfirmed:** what the trace looks like in Sentry's UI. Your screenshot will settle it.

## Things that are wrong (small fixes, I'll do them on your go)
1. **`twotoe brief` never fetches the CISA KEV feed.** Only the nightly workflow does, so the KEV check never fires on a manual run and `--offline` does nothing. The spec says `brief` refreshes the feed unless `--offline`. This matters for the real-machine run.
2. **The brief's footer still says "card: twotoe card (not built yet)".** The card has existed since Phase 5.
3. **The README says "Phases 0 to 5".**

## Things that would make Phase 8 claims untrue
4. **Your stopwatch baseline is already contaminated.** My Gate 1 and Gate 2 reports showed you what TwoToe finds on this machine: unpatched Node, the eMudhra root in Git and certifi, OpenCode installed. An honest baseline means either saying so in the post, or timing the manual triage on another machine.
5. **Real-machine scan scope.** Of TwoToe's default folders, only `~\Desktop` exists here. If your projects are under `<projects>`, scanning it also scans this repo's `eval/fixtures`, which contain synthetic litellm 1.107.0, `cook.pth` and `RAILWAY_TOKEN` on purpose. They would inflate the real counts. I need your real project folders, and I'd add an exclude option so the fixtures stay out.
6. **There is no 07:00 toast.** The video script (0:32) shows one, but the toast fires when the run finishes, around 03:01. Either cut that shot or I add a timer that waits until 7 a.m. (~1h).
7. **The writer's final numbers aren't settled.** In v2, gemma4:e4b needed the template for 14 of 80 briefs. Code should freeze after deciding on the v3 fix, which is one ~56-minute eval.
8. **The post's headline number needs care.** "Validator caught N invented facts" is 141 in v1 but 0 in v2, because v2's drafts had none. The post has to say which run it means.
9. **Sentry prize claim.** The research notes say past Sentry winners wrote up a real bug found through a trace. We haven't. The claim should rest only on what we built, or be dropped.
10. **The repo link in spec 17 (`SoumyaEXE/twotoe`) is wrong.** Your remote is `T-RexBytes/twotoe`.

## Things only you can do
11. **Recording:** asciinema doesn't run natively on Windows, and ffmpeg/gifski aren't installed. You can record with Snipping Tool, and I can convert the clips to GIFs if you approve installing ffmpeg (`winget install Gyan.FFmpeg`).

14. **The post:** spec 17 says the voice is yours and I proofread for facts only. I can draft the skeleton with every number filled in from the results files, for you to rewrite. DEV's rules also ask you to disclose AI assistance.
15. **Tag, push, publish:** these are public actions, so I'll only do them on your explicit go, after freeze. Your last commit (`356fadc`) is already pushed; nothing is uncommitted. The earliest deadline reading is Oct 25, 12:29 IST.

> my friend want to run this project on this latop so he is asking for the env, and i saw there is nothing for this project as env, but he is asking like there should've been something like temporal or something?..


### Claude (2026-10-22 16:05 UTC)

Your friend isn't missing anything: there's no env file because TwoToe doesn't need one. That's deliberate, since it never reads secret values, and everything it talks to runs on the laptop itself.

**What each part needs:**

| Part | Configured by | Env var needed? |
|---|---|---|
| Temporal | Local dev server on `127.0.0.1:7233`; the address is fixed to loopback in code. No account, no API key. | No |
| Ollama (the model) | Local server on `127.0.0.1:11434` | No. `TWOTOE_MODEL` is optional; the default is `gemma4:e4b` |
| Sentry | Optional; DSN in `~/.twotoe/config.json`, off by default | No |
| Project folders, region | Optional, in `~/.twotoe/config.json` | No |

`TWOTOE_MODEL` is the only env var TwoToe reads, and it's documented in `.env.example`.

The `OLLAMA_MODELS=D:\models` setting on your account belongs to Ollama, not TwoToe. It only changes where Ollama keeps model files.

**What your friend needs to install (once):**
1. Node 24.22.1 or newer, then `corepack enable --install-directory (npm config get prefix) pnpm`
2. Ollama, then `ollama pull gemma4:e4b`
3. The Temporal CLI, only for the nightly run or the crash test: `winget install Temporal.TemporalCLI`

**Then, in the repo:**
```powershell
pnpm install
pnpm tsx packages/cli/src/index.ts brief --no-llm --fixture eval/fixtures/f22-kitchen-sink   # no model needed
pnpm tsx packages/cli/src/index.ts brief --fixture eval/fixtures/f22-kitchen-sink            # with the local model
temporal server start-dev --db-filename "$HOME\.twotoe\temporal.db"                          # only for Temporal features
```

**On this laptop specifically:** everything above is already installed for your Windows account. If your friend uses your account, it just works, including your `~/.twotoe/config.json` (telemetry stays off unless they pass `--telemetry`). If they log in with their own Windows account, they need the Node/pnpm shim, and Ollama will look for models in its default folder rather than `D:\models` unless they set `OLLAMA_MODELS` for their account too.

If it helps others, I can put this into a "Running TwoToe" section in the README.

- **Simplest:** run `twotoe brief --save` when you sit down, then `twotoe card`.

**Pick one:**
1. **`twotoe sleep --taskscheduler` (Temporal), my recommendation.** At every log on, a Temporal dev server and a TwoToe worker start hidden. The worker creates the 3 a.m. schedule, and because your PC is off at night, the 18-hour catch-up runs the brief about a minute after you log in. This gives the post real "the nightly workflow ran" evidence for the Temporal category. Cost: two small background processes (roughly 200–300 MB RAM) whenever you're logged in.
2. **`twotoe sleep --no-temporal`.** One plain Windows task at 3 a.m. that can wake the PC from sleep, and runs at your next log on if missed. Lighter, but nothing from Temporal shows in the post.

### Claude (2026-10-22 17:02 UTC)

Nothing is running now. The v3 eval was stopped by Claude Code because your PC ran low on memory, but it got through 239 of its 240 briefs first, so the results are usable. I also found the real reason models kept writing over-long text, and fixed it; measuring that fix needs one more eval.

**What happened to the eval**
- Free RAM had dropped to 2.3 GB of 15.3 GB, with Ollama holding about 6 GB for a loaded model. Claude Code stopped the eval before its final save.
- I rebuilt the report from the per-brief files the eval writes as it goes. It names the one missing brief (qwen3:4b, run 5, kitchen-sink fixture) and says the wall time wasn't recorded.
- I've unloaded the idle model, so free RAM is back to 8 GB. The eval now unloads each model before starting the next, because Ollama can otherwise keep two models in memory at once.

**v3 results (`eval/RESULTS-v3.md`)**
- **gemma4:e4b:** drafts rejected 26% (48% in v2). Briefs needing the template fallback: 10 (v1 7, v2 14). Median 8.3s, down from 15.5s in v1.
- **gemma4:e2b:** drafts rejected 37% (96% in v1). Template fallbacks: 16 (v1 74).
- **qwen3:4b:** no better, 35 of 79 needed the template.
- **All models:** no invented or misplaced facts, in v2 or v3.

**The real leak, found and fixed**
- In v3 the model no longer sees the full summary, yet 87 drafts still contained it word for word.
- It was coming from the list of allowed words each finding carries: that list included the entire summary sentence, and the models copied it from there.
- The list now holds only the individual words and numbers. The validator checks the same things as before, and all 372 tests pass.
- This fix hasn't been measured yet. That's one more eval (v4) of about 45–55 minutes.

**For you to decide**
1. **Run the v4 eval now?** To avoid another memory stop, close Brave and VS Code while it runs. Without v4, the post would report v3 numbers and mention the fix as found but not yet measured.
2. **The nightly task (still pending):** "option 1" (Temporal) or "option 2" (Task Scheduler only), plus the folders your projects are in.

Saved: `docs/post/build-log.md` (v3 table, the memory stop, the leak) and `docs/DECISIONS.md`. Nothing is committed.

### Claude (2026-10-22 17:20 UTC)

The nightly Temporal setup is working now. Tonight's run is at 03:00 IST (21:30 UTC), and after that every night at the same time.

**What was wrong:** the worker task stopped about a second after it started. The hidden launcher used `*>>` to append output to a log file, with `$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'`. Windows PowerShell 5.1 treats a redirected program's stderr as errors. The Temporal SDK writes its normal INFO logs to stderr, so the first of those lines ended the script with code 0x1. That's why the log showed nothing after "schedule created".

**The fix** (`packages/cli/src/taskScheduler.ts`): the launcher now starts the program with `Start-Process` and redirects its output at the OS level. Normal output goes to `~/.twotoe/logs/<task>.log` and errors go to `<task>.err.log`. The script returns the program's own exit code. I added a test so the old `*>>` form can't come back.

**Checks I ran:**
- I re-registered both tasks and started `TwoToe-Worker` through Task Scheduler. It stays running, and its log shows `schedule updated` and `worker ready on twotoe`. The error log shows Temporal's `Worker state changed RUNNING`.
- The Temporal CLI lists the schedule's next runs as 2026-10-22T21:30Z and 2026-10-23T21:30Z.
- The CLI tests pass (30), and the typecheck is clean.
- Memory while idle: about 187 MB for the worker and 147 MB for the Temporal server, so roughly 335 MB together. That's more than my earlier guess of about 150 MB.

**Things to know:**
- The log files are now replaced each time a task starts. You only see the latest run, not a history.
- The Temporal server task is still the one started before the fix. That's fine: it's running and reachable. It switches to the new launcher at your next logon.
- I stopped the worker I had started by hand, so only the scheduled one is running now.
- The scan only covers the default folders, and on your machine only `~\Desktop` exists. To include your project folders, add a `"roots": [...]` list to `~/.twotoe/config.json`. Tonight's brief will be thin without it.
- To remove everything: `twotoe sleep --uninstall`.

### Claude (2026-10-23 13:40 UTC)

Yes, those two windows came from TwoToe. They were the logon tasks for the Temporal server and the worker. I've fixed it, and the next logon should open no windows.

**Why they showed up:** your PC uses Windows Terminal as its default console. Windows Terminal ignores PowerShell's "hidden window" flag, so each of the two tasks opened a visible terminal window.

**What I changed** (`packages/cli/src/taskScheduler.ts`): the tasks now start through `conhost.exe --headless`, a built-in Windows console host that never creates a window. The program the launcher starts shares that hidden console instead of opening its own.

**Checks I ran:**
- I re-registered both tasks, stopped the running worker and server, and restarted them through Task Scheduler the same way a logon does. No new terminal windows or processes appeared. Both tasks are in the Running state.
- The worker log shows `schedule updated` and `worker ready`, so tonight's 03:00 run is still set.
- The CLI tests pass (30), including new checks for the headless launch. The typecheck is clean.

The one thing I couldn't test directly is a real logon, because that means signing out. Starting the tasks by hand runs the same command, so I expect no windows next time. If any still appear, tell me.

To remove the nightly tasks entirely, run `twotoe sleep --uninstall`. Like the earlier fix, this change isn't committed yet.

function parseVersion(v: string): number[] {
  return v.replace(/^v/, "").split(".").map((n) => Number.parseInt(n, 10) || 0);
}

// SPEC 8.2.1 dogfood check: is the Node running TwoToe itself patched?
export function selfNodeStatus(version: string = process.version): { version: string; patched: boolean | null; fixed: string | null } {
  const node = loadPack().advisories.find((a) => a.id === "nodejs-2026-10-21");
  const fixed = (node?.check.params.fixed ?? {}) as Record<string, string>;
  const [major = 0, minor = 0, patch = 0] = parseVersion(version);
  const target = fixed[String(major)];
  if (!target) return { version: version.replace(/^v/, ""), patched: null, fixed: null };
  const [, tMinor = 0, tPatch = 0] = parseVersion(target);
  const patched = minor > tMinor || (minor === tMinor && patch >= tPatch);
  return { version: version.replace(/^v/, ""), patched, fixed: target };
}

I checked the code against every section of SPEC.md. The spec items not done fall into four groups: submission steps, features not built, gaps in testing and measurement, and facts not yet verified. Nothing breaks a hard rule.

## 1. Submission steps (Phase 8, required) not done yet

| Item | Why not done |
|---|---|
| Stopwatch the manual triage baseline | Only you can do it, and it has to happen before you see TwoToe's real results. |
| Real-machine run for the post's numbers | The first real nightly run is tonight at 03:00. It only scans `~\Desktop` unless you add `roots` to your config. |
| Terminal GIF, crash-test clip, Sentry screenshot, card-on-phone screenshot | These need you to record them. |
| The DEV post | It's waiting on the recordings and final numbers. Plan: I draft a skeleton, you rewrite it, then I fact-check it. |
| Tag `v1.0-submission` and publish | Waiting on your go. |
| Card hosted on twotoe.tech (Gate 5) | You deferred the domain and the DigitalOcean deploy. One deploy setting is also unconfirmed: whether DigitalOcean's builder offers Node 24.22.1. |
| v4 eval | My last leak fix is unmeasured. Before it, every finding's allowed-words list included its whole summary sentence. The published numbers (RESULTS v3) come from the code before that fix. You haven't decided whether to run it. |

## 2. Spec features not built

| Item | Spec status | Why not |
|---|---|---|
| CLI commands `doctor`, `explain`, `pack`, `eval` | Listed in sections 4.2 and 12 | No phase prompt or gate asked for them, and I missed them. Nobody decided to drop them. The eval runs through `tsx eval/run-eval.ts` instead. `doctor` would be the most useful of the four. |
| `brief --open` flag | Section 12 | Not built; `twotoe card` does the same job. |
| macOS `--launchd` | SHOULD | No Mac to test on. |
| Windows toast at 07:00 | SHOULD | Cut by decision (your PC isn't on at night). A toast at the end of the run exists, but it's off by default. |
| Blind readability check (template vs model) | SHOULD | Needs two people to rank briefs blind. |
| Mastra "ask", ElevenLabs voice, Arduino LED | STRETCH | Stretch goals wait until the post draft exists. |

## 3. Gaps in testing and measurement

- **CI not confirmed.** The CI config runs on both windows-latest and ubuntu-latest, but I can't see whether it passes because the GitHub CLI isn't installed here. Everything since `356fadc` is uncommitted, so CI hasn't run on it. The README also has no CI badge.
- **No coverage check.** The spec targets 90% line coverage in `core` and `writer`. No coverage tool is set up, so this has never been measured.
- **End-to-end test is close but not exact.** The spec asks for a snapshot of `brief --fixture eval/fixtures/f22-kitchen-sink --no-llm`. The existing test runs an equivalent temporary fixture and checks the fields instead.

## 4. Facts not yet verified (from `docs/VERIFY.md`)

- **One question for you:** should the eMudhra check also look for "emSign Root TLS CA - G3" and "emSign Root CS CA - G3"? Bugzilla files the compromised intermediates under those two names. The open eMudhra item below hinges on this.
- How Microsoft's block of the eMudhra root shows up in the Windows certificate store. No Microsoft source found, so Windows-store matches stay "possible".
- Two claims were dropped from the pack because I couldn't confirm them from a source:
  - the GitLab CVE-2026-97229 precondition (it comes from Rapid7, which I didn't fetch);
  - LiteLLM's "hourly backdoor" wording.
- LiteLLM has no CVE ID in any source I read.
- SBI and OpenCode rely on secondary sources. The SBI filing PDF returned 403, and I didn't fetch OpenCode's own post.
- Some detection paths are untested because the software isn't on your machine:
  - Plex's version field;
  - Microsoft Store Python, pipx and uv paths.
- The spec (section 7.1) says to re-verify every fact before tagging and again on publish day. That hasn't been done yet.

Several intended departures from the spec are logged in `docs/DECISIONS.md`. Examples: an 18-hour catch-up window instead of 6, telemetry settings in the config file instead of env vars, and self-hosted card fonts. They aren't gaps.

While checking, I found two of my own docs out of date and fixed them. `docs/VERIFY.md` still said `conhost --headless` was unused. `docs/DECISIONS.md` said the scheduled tasks would only be registered at code freeze. Both now match what's running.

The quickest things to close before the freeze are the eMudhra question, a decision on the v4 eval, and whether you want `doctor` and the other three commands built or listed as not built in the post.

export const TASK_QUEUE = "twotoe";

// Temporal gRPC must stay on this machine (SPEC 15.1).
export function assertLoopbackAddress(address: string): void {
  const host = normalizeHost(address.replace(/:\d+$/, ""));
  if (!LOOPBACK_HOSTS.has(host)) throw new Error(`Temporal address must be loopback, got ${host}`);
}

// temporal.exe on PATH, or where winget puts it (a fresh install is not on
// the PATH of shells that were already open).
export async function findTemporalExe(home: string = os.homedir()): Promise<string | null> {
  const onPath = (await whichAll("temporal")).find((p) => /temporal(\.exe)?$/i.test(p));
  if (onPath) return onPath;
  const winget = path.join(home, "AppData", "Local", "Microsoft", "WinGet", "Links", "temporal.exe");
  return fs.existsSync(winget) ? winget : null;
}

  packVersion: z.string(),

}).superRefine((pack, ctx) => {
  const seen = new Set<string>();
  pack.advisories.forEach((a, i) => {
    if (seen.has(a.id)) {
      ctx.addIssue({ code: z.ZodIssueCode.custom, path: ["advisories", i, "id"],
                     message: `duplicate advisory id ${a.id}` });
    }
    seen.add(a.id);
  });
});

export function expandHome(p: string, home: string = os.homedir()): string {
  return p === "~" || p.startsWith("~/") || p.startsWith("~\\") ? path.join(home, p.slice(2)) : p;
}

// SPEC 8.3 default roots on Windows (only those that exist are scanned).
export function defaultRoots(home: string = os.homedir()): string[] {
  return [
    ["code"], ["projects"], ["dev"], ["Documents", "GitHub"], ["source", "repos"], ["Desktop"],
  ].map((segs) => path.join(home, ...segs)).filter((p) => fs.existsSync(p));
}

// Risky-token extraction (SPEC 10.5). The matcher builds allowedTokens with
// this exact function and the validator checks model text with it, so both
// walls agree on what counts as a fact.

export const KNOWN_VENDORS = [
  "Node.js", "Node", "PHP", "Plex", "GitLab", "LiteLLM", "Railway", "OpenCode", "OpenAI",
  "Anthropic", "Google", "eMudhra", "SBI", "CISA",
];

// SPEC 10.5 says \d{4,}; any length is stricter, so an invented "CVE-2026-1" is caught too.
const CVE_RE = /CVE-\d{4}-\d+/gi;
const VERSION_RE = /\b\d+(?:\.\d+){1,3}\b/g;
const NUMBER_RE = /\b\d{2,}\b/g;
const VENDOR_RE = new RegExp(`\\b(?:${KNOWN_VENDORS.map((v) => v.replace(/\./g, "\\.")).join("|")})\\b`, "g");

export function extractRiskyTokens(text: string): string[] {
  const out = new Set<string>();
  for (const re of [CVE_RE, VERSION_RE, NUMBER_RE, VENDOR_RE]) {
    for (const m of text.matchAll(re)) out.add(m[0]);
  }
  return [...out];
}

export function normToken(t: string): string {
  return t.trim().toLowerCase();
}

// Every given string plus every risky token inside it, deduped (case-insensitive).

// Evidence locations go to the model project-relative, never with a home
// path: "~\code\rail\.env" under root "~\code" -> "rail\.env".
export function relativeLocation(location: string, roots: string[]): string {
  const prefixed = location.match(/^([a-z][a-z-]+:)(.+)$/i);   // "certifi:~\...", not "C:\..."
  if (prefixed && /^[~\\/]|^[A-Za-z]:/.test(prefixed[2]!)) return prefixed[1]! + relativeLocation(prefixed[2]!, roots);
  const lower = location.toLowerCase();
  for (const r of roots) {
    const rl = r.toLowerCase();
    if (lower.startsWith(rl) && /^[\\/]/.test(location.slice(r.length))) return location.slice(r.length + 1);
  }
  if (/^~|^[A-Za-z]:[\\/]|^[\\/]/.test(location)) {
    const parts = location.split(/[\\/]/).filter(Boolean);
    return parts.slice(-3).join("\\");
  }
  return location;
}

// SPEC 6 rule: the model sees only these fields. No raw file contents, no

// allowedTokens). `kev` is added because rule 4 refers to it.

+   let line = "";
+   for (const word of text.split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean)) {
+     if (line && indent.length + line.length + 1 + word.length > width) { lines.push(line); line = word; }
+     else line = line ? `${line} ${word}` : word;
+   }
+   if (line) lines.push(line);
+   return lines.map((l, i) => (i === 0 ? `  ${label.padEnd(12)}${l}` : `${indent}${l}`));
+ }

// Bolds the first whole-token occurrence ("21" must not light up inside "2026").
function highlight(text: string, token: string): string {
  const esc = token.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, "\\$&");
  const m = new RegExp(`(?<![\\w.])${esc}(?![\\w.]*\\d)`).exec(text);
  return m ? `${text.slice(0, m.index)}**${token}**${text.slice(m.index + token.length)}` : text;
}

+     if (line && 2 + line.length + 1 + word.length > width) { lines.push(`  ${line}`); line = word; }
+     else line = line ? `${line} ${word}` : word;
+   }
+   if (line) lines.push(`  ${line}`);
+   return lines;
+ }
+ 
+ export function renderAnswer(r: AskResult, color = true): string {
+   const dim = color ? pc.dim : (s: string) => s;
+   const lines = [...wrapIndented(r.answer), ""];
```

<details><summary>PowerShell: Read the redaction helpers</summary>

```
import os from "node:os";

function escapeRe(s: string): string {
  return s.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, "\\$&");
}

// Replaces home directories with "~" in any text: the real home (as written,
// with forward slashes, and JSON-escaped), then any other C:\Users\<name>,
// ~ or ~ Short 8.3 names (SOURIS~1) are caught by the
// generic patterns.
export function redactText(text: string, home: string = os.homedir()): string {
  let out = text;
  if (home && home.length > 3) {
    const variants = new Set([
      home,
      home.replace(/\\/g, "/"),
      home.replace(/\\/g, "\\\\"),
      home.replace(/\//g, "\\"),
    ]);
    for (const v of [...variants].sort((a, b) => b.length - a.length)) {
      // Boundary check so ~ never eats the start of ~
      out = out.replace(new RegExp(`${escapeRe(v)}(?=[\\\\/"'\\s:;,)\\]}]|$)`, "gi"), "~");
    }
  }
  return out
    .replace(/\b[A-Za-z]:(?:\\\\|\\|\/)Users(?:\\\\|\\|\/)[^\\/"'\s:*?<>|]+/gi, "~")
    .replace(/\/Users\/[^/"'\s]+/g, "~")
    .replace(/\/home\/[^/"'\s]+/g, "~");
}

export const redactPath = redactText;
```

- // activityType name -> attempts reported by ActivityTaskStarted events.
+ // All history text: event fields plus every payload's bytes decoded as UTF-8.
+ function historyText(history: unknown): string {
+   const parts: string[] = [];
+   const walk = (v: unknown): void => {
+     if (v instanceof Uint8Array) { parts.push(Buffer.from(v).toString("utf8")); return; }
+     if (Array.isArray(v)) { v.forEach(walk); return; }
+     if (v && typeof v === "object") { for (const x of Object.values(v)) walk(x); return; }
+     if (typeof v === "string") parts.push(v);
+   };
+   walk(history);
+   return parts.join("\n");
+ }

import { assertLoopbackAddress, TASK_QUEUE, TEMPORAL_ADDRESS } from "./temporal";

export async function withClient<T>(fn: (client: Client) => Promise<T>, address: string = TEMPORAL_ADDRESS): Promise<T> {
  assertLoopbackAddress(address);
  const connection = await Connection.connect({ address });
  try {
    return await fn(new Client({ connection, identity: "twotoe" }));
  } finally {
    await connection.close();
  }
}

}

## Bugs the screenshot work uncovered (all fixed and tested)

- **Your home path and PC name were stored in Temporal's history** (the nightly schedule's input, activity results, the worker's name), and they show in Temporal's web UI. The test meant to catch this could never fail, because it searched the stored data without decoding it.
- **`doctor`'s pre-warm didn't warm the model.** The first brief after it took 45 s; now 29.5 s.
- **A safety hole in the network allowlist.** If two allowlist guards were installed one inside the other, removing the inner one left nothing in force. No TwoToe command does this; my screenshot script did.
- **An empty-quote bug in the eval report.**

### Claude (2026-10-23 15:32 UTC)

The red crosses are fixed, and the codebase is ready to hand over. I put the files in `docs/blog/`, reading "blod" as a typo.

**Why CI was failing.** Git was ignoring the test fixtures' `.env` files, because the repo-wide `.env` ignore rule caught them too. They only hold the canary value and `fixture-not-a-token`, but without them a fresh clone loses the Railway finding, and the f22 snapshot test failed on both CI jobs. I reproduced that in a fresh clone, committed the files, and ran a second fresh clone with CI's exact steps: typecheck clean, all 412 tests pass, coverage passes. I can't open your GitHub logs or run Ubuntu here, so check that the next run shows green checks; the Ubuntu job hit the same missing files, so it should be fixed too.

**What your friend gets** (pushed as `5e3bea9`):
- **`docs/blog/info.md`**, the single handover file:
  - challenge rules, deadline and tags;
  - which prize categories you can honestly claim;
  - the fact-check table with source links;
  - every quotable number with the file it comes from;
  - the eval story and the honest list of what broke;
  - Sentry details, including that the demo rejection was forced;
  - an inventory of all 26 images saying what each shows and where it fits;
  - the publish checklist.
- **`docs/blog/dummy-post.md`**, a complete sample post with images in place. Everything not measured yet is marked `[DUMMY: ...]` so a made-up number can't slip into the published post.
- **`scripts/blog/`**, the scripts that made every screenshot, GIF, clip and the chart. Before this they lived only in my temporary folder, so your friend couldn't have regenerated a single image. They're in the repo now with no machine paths, and they reproduce the committed images byte for byte.
- **`eval/out-v4/`**, a frozen copy (0.4 MB) of the v4 eval's raw output, which git normally ignores. Your friend can recheck the "79 of 95" numbers and build the blind sheet without a 39-minute GPU run.
- A README link pointing straight to `info.md`.

**Things your friend can't get from the repo.** `info.md` lists each one with what to do. The ones that need you before you hand over:
- **The repo is still private.** It has to be public for the submission, and your friend needs access.
- **Your Claude Code session transcript** is only on this PC. It's needed for "My Agent Session" and maybe the Entire category, and it contains real paths, so redact it before sharing.
- **The Sentry trace** sits in your Sentry account (org `none-0un`). The screenshots are already committed. Your `~/.twotoe/config.json` with the DSN stays on your PC, which is correct.
- **Tonight's real nightly result** on your PC feeds the "I fixed k things" line. Share aggregate counts only.
- **The stopwatch baseline and the blind readers** both still need doing.

The rest (the built card, the local models, the Temporal data, the crash-test leftovers) can be rebuilt on any machine, and `info.md` gives the command for each.
